messages:
Elena Support: FYI support ticket from a high-value customer — they hit repeated 502/504s and long tail latencies for hosted inference in us-west-1 starting ~11:58 PDT. Customer attached sample request ids: r_8a3f..., r_8a41... and a video screencap. They're asking for impact window and workaround.
Marta SRE: Pulling graphs now. I see a sharp 5xx spike at 11:59 and a simultaneous RTT increase for the us-west-1 edge fleet. Request success rate down from 99.9% -> 92% for a ~6m window. Adding to incident channel. @Ibrahim can you check infra egress?
Ibrahim Netops: Looking. BGP sessions to transit peer X show flaps starting 11:58:22. Also seeing packet loss concentrated on path via provider-as34567 to west-edge-pop-a. Running mtr from edge host:
```
Start: host-edge-a01 (10.0.12.41)                      2026-03-15T11:59:05Z
HOST: host-edge-a01                   Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 1.|-- 10.0.12.41                     0.0%    10    0.3   0.4   0.2   1.1   0.2
 2.|-- 172.16.5.2                     0.0%    10    1.1   1.3   1.0   2.4   0.4
 3.|-- 198.51.100.53                 18.0%    10   12.4  15.8   2.1  62.6  18.2
 4.|-- 198.51.100.57                 38.0%    10   25.9  28.1  10.2  70.2  19.6
 5.|-- 203.0.113.21                  36.0%    10   23.8  24.5  11.8  51.7  11.1
```
This looks like provider path micro-loss/jitter beyond our edge-to-transit hop.
Samir Eng: Repro steps for API team: I can repro 502 locally by replaying a recorded call with header x-request-id=r_8a3f... against ausw1 gateway — it times out waiting on upstream inference pool. Adding tcpdump on gateway to capture SYN/ACK failures.
Elena Support: Customer asked if this is an auth/billing issue — they see 502, not 401/402. Confirmed not billing.
Marta SRE: Confirmed not code rollback; deploy-bot shows no ingress changes, last deploy ~10:05 PDT.
Ibrahim Netops: I've opened NOC ticket with provider (AS34567) — they acknowledge a partial egress congestion and are investigating an overloaded egress link in us-west region. Provider assigned case 987654. I've requested emergency reroute or prepull of alternate peering.
Samir Eng: Short mitigation ideas: (1) divert traffic to us-west-2b edge-pop which still shows healthy paths, (2) throttle long-running requests and enable faster fallback to lower token limits to reduce queueing, (3) enable cached KV prefix hits for warm sessions. Which is realistic quickly?
Marta SRE: We can flip routing policy for the affected customer to prefer us-west-2b via smart routing rule; need approval from support for per-customer routing change and to avoid cross-AZ consistency issues. @Elena can you ask customer if they accept a brief routing switchover? Also preparing canary config to reduce concurrency to inference pools to limit head-of-line blocking.
Elena Support: Customer agreed to try routing to alternate edge in the same region — they want minimal traffic loss. Doing it now.
deploy-bot: route-change: applying routing policy override for customer-id cust_0923 -> prefer edge-pop us-west-2b (commit a3f4b).
Marta SRE: Route change applied. Observability: success rate for that customer's keys rose from 86% -> 98% in the next 90s. Latency tail improved. Rolling the override for other impacted customers with the same prefix.
Ibrahim Netops: Provider just responded: 'we see localized egress microbursts and do a partial traffic engineering change, monitoring. ETA 20-30m for full stabilization.' They've filtered a flapping upstream peer.
Samir Eng: Notes for root cause DB: provider AS34567 egress micro-loss due to overloaded POP switch + transient BGP withdrawal causing asymmetry; symptoms: 502/504 and long upstream wait times in hosted inference (the runtime waits on responses from model pool, upstream connection resets). Repro steps:
1) from edge host: curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.us-west-1:443:<edge-ip> "POST /v1/completions" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d @payload.json (use recorded payload).
2) if intermittent 502, run tcpdump: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <upstream-ip> and tcp` and capture 30s window.
3) run mtr to provider next-hop to see loss patterns.
```
# tcpdump sample (trimmed)
15:59:24.123456 IP host-edge-a01.54712 > 198.51.100.53.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
15:59:24.124001 IP 198.51.100.53.443 > host-edge-a01.54712: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```
Ibrahim Netops: After provider applied traffic engineering, our interleaved mtr now shows loss back to <1% and no BGP flaps for 6m.
Marta SRE: Observability shows 5xx rate returning to baseline. I'll keep the routing override active for 30m then revert once provider confirms full stabilization.
Elena Support: Customer updated: 'We're seeing much better now, thanks. Please confirm root cause and postmortem.' I told them we'll follow up with timeline and RCA.
provider-noc-bot: Case 987654 - provider report: 'transit POP in west region experienced control-plane CPU spike causing partial packet drops to some peers; emergency TE mitigated by shifting sessions to alternate spine. No config change on Redwood side required.'
Marta SRE: Post-incident actions: 1) add probe alerts for >5% egress loss to provider next-hop (currently we only alert on BGP down), 2) add automated per-customer routing overrides for high-tier customers to failover to alternate edge-pop, 3) document runbook steps for probe collection (mtr/tcpdump/traceroute) and support messaging template.
Samir Eng: Also will add runtime protection to detect repeated upstream SYN resets and fall back faster to model-variant that is local to the edge.
Ibrahim Netops: Closing provider case after 2h monitoring; they confirm stable.
Marta SRE: Marking incident RESOLVED for now. Will file full postmortem with timeline and impact numbers.
Elena Support: Thanks team — I sent customer update and credit offer. Closing support ticket after PM posts RCA. :white_check_mark:
